DISCRIMINATING: 'Diaporthe' vs 'Phytophthora'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. a continuous dark brown lesion extending upward from the taproot
Diaporthe: Diaporthe (pod and stem blight) produces distinctive linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems; stem canker form shows sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins near lower-canopy nodes and may show internal black zone lines.
Phytophthora: Phytophthora produces a solid dark brown lesion originating at the taproot and extending upward along the lower stem, potentially girdling the stem and causing stunting, yellowing, or death.
Decision rule  : IF the lower stem shows a continuous dark brown discoloration extending upward from the taproot (no discrete specks), THEN suspect Phytophthora; IF the stem surface displays linear rows of discrete black specks (pycnidia) or sunken cankers with reddish margins at nodes, THEN suspect Diaporthe.

DISCRIMINATING: 'Diaporthe' vs 'Phomopsis'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. chalky white mold on cracked/shriveled seeds
Diaporthe: Diaporthe produces sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins on lower stems, and most distinctively, linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems; interior of lower stems may show irregular thin black 'zone' lines.
Phomopsis: Phomopsis is characterized by cracked, shriveled seeds covered with chalky white mold, and infected seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.
Decision rule  : IF black specks arranged in linear rows are visible on mature stems, suspect Diaporthe (pod and stem blight); IF seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold or seedlings show pinpoint reddish-brown lesions on cotyledons, suspect Phomopsis seed/seedling infection.

DISCRIMINATING: 'Phytophthora' vs 'Phomopsis'
Ruling feature : Lesion color and location: dark brown girdling lesion extending up from taproot (Disease A) vs. reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or streaks near soil line with chalky white mold on seeds (Disease B)
Phytophthora: A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending upward from the taproot, potentially reaching several nodes and girdling the stem, leading to stunting or death. No white mold or cotyledon lesions are described.
Phomopsis: Cracked, shriveled seeds covered with chalky white mold; seedlings exhibit reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.
Decision rule  : IF the lower stem shows a dark brown girdling lesion tracking up from the taproot (no white mold, no cotyledon spots), THEN suspect Phytophthora (Disease A); IF seeds are shriveled with chalky white mold and/or seedlings have reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or streaks near the soil line, THEN suspect Phomopsis (Disease B).
